newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA, BECKHAM ON TARGET IN DULL DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA, BECKHAM ON TARGET IN DULL DRAW.

text.p: Italy's Gianfranco Zola and England's David Beckham scored a goal apiece as Chelsea drew 1-1 with Manchester United in a lacklustre English premier league match on Saturday.
Zola, in spectacular form since his move to west London from Parma, put Chelsea ahead with a cheeky goal after just two minutes.

He latched on to a pass down the right flank from Dan Petrescu, took the ball to the touchline, fooled fullback Denis Irwin, strolled past a leaden-footed Gary Pallister and beat Peter Schmeichel on his inside post with embarrassing ease.

The goal typified United's first half performance. Pallister and Ronny Johnsen looked hesitant at the back and Roy Keane, standing in as captain for the suspended Eric Cantona, was rapidly losing his temper.
The contrast with Wednesday night, when the champions ripped Arsenal apart in the first 45 minutes of their league clash, was marked.

Chelsea could have doubled their lead after 11 minutes when Zola ran at the heart of the United defence and freed Mark Hughes with a subtle reverse pass, but the former United striker scuffed his shot and Schmeichel saved easily.
United improved after they tinkered with their formation, pushing Brian McClair into attack alongside Norwegian Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Andy Cole -- scorers in United's 2-1 midweek win at Highbury.
"After we went to three up front we dominated the game," defender Gary Neville said afterwards. "In the first half I think we played four or five different systems.
"It's been a good week for us. We've had two tough games in London and we've got four points."
McClair started to trouble the home defence and Solskjaer forced a save from Kevin Hitchcock with a powerful strike from a tight angle just before the break.
Chelsea had to substitute Hitchcock early in the second period after he failed to shake off a shoulder injury picked up in the first half.
He was replaced by Norway's Frode Grodas, making his first appearance in five matches.
United continued to threaten and finally equalised after 68 minutes, courtesy of a typically clinical strike from Beckham.

Neville swung in an innocuous looking cross from the right, Chelsea defender Eddie Sinclair headed the ball skywards, and when it fell Beckham crashed home a crisp volley off the underside of the bar.
McClair fired two long-range strikes just over shortly afterwards and Cole headed just over as United pressed for a winner.
But the game petered to a close with the score at 1-1, a result which left Chelsea sixth, 12 points behind United with two games in hand.

Chelsea - 13-Kevin Hitchcock (30-Frode Grodas 52), 2-Dan Petrescu (4-Ruud Gullit 77), 5-Franck Leboeuf, 6-Steve Clarke, 10-Mark Hughes, 11-Dennis Wise, 16-Roberto di Matteo, 20-Frank Sinclair, 24-Eddy Newton, 25-Gianfranco Zola, 17-Scott Minto (18-Erland Johnsen 71).

Man Utd - 1-Peter Schmeichel, 2-Gary Neville, 3-Denis Irwin, 6-Gary Pallister, 9-Andy Cole, 10-David Beckham, 11-Ryan Giggs (Jordi Cruyff 86), 13-Brian McClair, 16-Roy Keane, 19-Ronny Johnsen (4-David May 89), 20-Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.
